Fix \(r\in(0,1)\), \(w\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta>0\).  Put
\[
T_\theta(z)=\frac{\theta z}{1+(\theta-1)z},\qquad
f_\theta(z)=(1-w)z+wT_\theta(z),\qquad 0\leq z\leq1.
\]
The denominator in \(T_\theta\) is \(1-z+\theta z>0\), and
\[
T_\theta'(z)=\frac{\theta}{\{1+(\theta-1)z\}^2}>0,\qquad
f_\theta'(z)=(1-w)+wT_\theta'(z)>0.
\]
Moreover, \(f_\theta(0)=0\) and \(f_\theta(1)=1\).  The intermediate-value theorem and strict monotonicity therefore give exactly one \(m_0\in(0,1)\) such that \(f_\theta(m_0)=r\), and then \(m_1=T_\theta(m_0)\in(0,1)\) is unique.

Multiplication by the strictly positive denominator \(1+(\theta-1)m_0\) gives, without introducing an extraneous solution,
\[
(1-w)(\theta-1)m_0^2+\bigl[1+(w-r)(\theta-1)\bigr]m_0-r=0.
\]
Write \(B=1+(w-r)(\theta-1)\) and \(D=B^2+4(1-w)(\theta-1)r\).  If \(\theta=1\), the displayed equation is \(m_0-r=0\).  If \(\theta\neq1\), the unique feasible root, including the linear case \(w=1\), is
\[
m_0=\frac{2r}{B+\sqrt D}.
\]
Indeed, when \(w<1\) this is the quadratic root obtained by rationalizing \((-B+\sqrt D)/\{2(1-w)(\theta-1)\}\), and uniqueness of the root in \((0,1)\) selects its nonnegative square root.  Its denominator is positive: for \(\theta>1\) and \(w<1\), \(D>B^2\); for \(\theta<1\), \(B=1-(w-r)(1-\theta)>0\); and for \(w=1\), \(B=r+(1-r)\theta>0\) and \(D=B^2\).  Thus this root is exactly \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\) from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mixture\text{-}root}\), including its removable value at \(\theta=1\), and the claimed mixture identity follows from \(f_\theta(m_0)=r\).

Fix an arm and stratum and suppress those indices.  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\), write \(m_0=\operatorname{expit}(s)\), \(m_1=\operatorname{expit}(s+t)\), and \(t=\log\theta\), where \(s\) is uniquely chosen so that
\[
r=(1-w)m_0+wm_1.
\]
Let \(v_j=m_j(1-m_j)>0\).  Differentiation at fixed \(r\) is legitimate because \((1-w)v_0+wv_1>0\), and gives
\[
0=\{(1-w)v_0+wv_1\}\frac{ds}{dt}+wv_1,
\qquad
\frac{ds}{dt}=-\frac{wv_1}{(1-w)v_0+wv_1}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{d(m_1-m_0)}{dt}
=v_1\left(1+\frac{ds}{dt}\right)-v_0\frac{ds}{dt}
=\frac{v_0v_1}{(1-w)v_0+wv_1}>0.
\]
This calculation also covers \(w=0\) and \(w=1\).  Since \(dt/d\theta=1/\theta>0\), \(m_1-m_0\) is strictly increasing in \(\theta\).

On the positive chart, the outcome joint-cell cross-product ratio is
\[
\frac{\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}}
     {\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}}
=\frac{m_1(1-m_0)}{m_0(1-m_1)}=\theta,
\]
because the positive factors \(\widetilde P(U=u,X=x)\) cancel.  Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) are therefore exactly \(\Gamma_a^{-1}\leq\theta\leq\Gamma_a\).

Finally, the observed arm mixture and the marginal-\(U\) mixture are respectively
\[
r=(1-w)m_0+wm_1,
\qquad
q=(1-\pi)m_0+\pi m_1.
\]
Subtracting yields
\[
q-r=(\pi-w)(m_1-m_0).
\]
Thus \(q\) is increasing in \(\theta\) when \(\pi-w>0\), decreasing when \(\pi-w<0\), and constant when \(\pi=w\).  Its minimum and maximum over the closed odds-budget interval are consequently attained at \(\Gamma_a^{-1}\) and \(\Gamma_a\), in the order stated in the lemma; equality in the sign condition merely makes either endpoint an admissible choice.

For any fixed \(c>0\), as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\),
\[
\operatorname{OR}(c\varepsilon,\varepsilon)
=\frac{c(1-\varepsilon)}{1-c\varepsilon}\longrightarrow c.
\]
Distinct values of \(c\) give distinct limits at \((0,0)\).  Likewise,
\[
\operatorname{OR}(1-c\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)
=\frac{1-c\varepsilon}{c(1-\varepsilon)}\longrightarrow c^{-1},
\]
so no path-independent continuous extension exists at \((1,1)\).  Hence the odds-ratio coordinate \(\theta_{a,x}\) is properly confined to \(\mathcal M^\circ\).

For fixed \(r\in(0,1)\) and finite \(\theta>0\), the proof of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) represents \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\) as the unique inverse of the continuous, strictly increasing map \(f_\theta\).  Its displayed radical formula has positive denominator also at \(w=0,1\), and therefore is continuous in \(w\in[0,1]\); the value at \(\theta=1\) is its removable limit \(r\).  It follows from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}adjusted\text{-}arm\text{-}mean}\) that \(q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\) is continuous on \([0,1]^2\), because \(\pi_x=p_xw_1+(1-p_x)w_0\) is affine and every displayed denominator is positive.

The region \(D_{A,x}\) is the intersection of \([0,1]^2\) with two inverse images of \(({-}\infty,0]\) under polynomials, hence it is closed and compact.  A minimum or maximum of two continuous functions is continuous, since
\[
\min(f,g)=\frac{f+g-|f-g|}{2},
\qquad
\max(f,g)=\frac{f+g+|f-g|}{2}.
\]
Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}endpoints}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) now imply that \(q^-_{a,x}\), \(q^+_{a,x}\), \(H_x^-\), and \(H_x^+\) extend continuously to all of \(D_{A,x}\).  At a constant-confounder corner \((w_0,w_1)=(c,c)\), with \(c\in\{0,1\}\), one has \(\pi_x=w_{a,x}=c\), so the identity
\[
q_{a,x}-r_{a,x}=(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(m_1-m_0)
\]
gives \(q_{a,x}=r_{a,x}\) for every finite \(\theta\).  Thus the compact probability-scale objective is well defined at precisely the corners where the odds-ratio chart itself is not.

Work first under a law in \(\mathcal M^\circ\).  Strict positivity makes every conditional probability below lie in \((0,1)\).  Define
\[
e_{u,x}=\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=u,X=x),
\qquad
\alpha_x=\operatorname{logit}(e_{1,x})-\operatorname{logit}(e_{0,x}).
\]
Then, with \(b_x=\operatorname{logit}(e_{0,x})\),
\[
\operatorname{logit}\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=u,X=x)=b_x+\alpha_xu.
\]
Cancellation of the positive \(U,X\) margins gives
\[
e^{\alpha_x}
=\frac{\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}}
       {\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}}.
\]
Thus Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) hold if and only if \(|\alpha_x|\leq\log\Gamma_A\).

Similarly, latent ignorability from Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}ignorability}\) permits the arm-specific conditional risks to be written without conditioning on \(A\).  Define
\[
\delta_{a,x}=\operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,1,x})-
              \operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,0,x}),
\qquad
c_{a,x}=\operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,0,x}).
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{logit}\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid U=u,X=x\}
=c_{a,x}+\delta_{a,x}u,
\]
and cancellation of the positive \(U,X\) margins yields
\[
e^{\delta_{a,x}}
=\frac{\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}}
       {\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}}.
\]
The two outcome inequalities are therefore equivalent to \(|\delta_{a,x}|\leq\log\Gamma_a\).  The intercepts \(b_x,c_{a,x}\) remain unrestricted except for the observed-margin equations.  This proves both inclusions between \(\mathcal M^\circ\) and the stated union of positive binary-logistic families.

For completeness, consider the closure claim in probability-table coordinates.  Observed-margin compatibility is affine; consistency is imposed by the deterministic map \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\); latent ignorability is the collection of finite-table cross-product equalities; and all four odds restrictions are the displayed weak polynomial inequalities.  Their common solution set \(C\subset\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}\) is closed.  Hence \(\mathcal M\subseteq C\).

For the reverse inclusion, take a table in \(C\).  In each stratum its treatment-confounder table is represented by its posterior pair \((w_0,w_1)\in D_{A,x}\).  For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), set
\[
w_a^{(\varepsilon)}=(1-\varepsilon)w_a+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}.
\]
The map \(T_\varepsilon(v)=(1-\varepsilon)v+\varepsilon/2\) contracts log-odds differences, because
\[
T_\varepsilon(v)\{1-T_\varepsilon(v)\}
\geq(1-\varepsilon)v(1-v),
\qquad
\left|\frac{d\operatorname{logit}T_\varepsilon(v)}
{d\operatorname{logit}v}\right|\leq1.
\]
Thus \((w_0^{(\varepsilon)},w_1^{(\varepsilon)})\in D_{A,x}\cap(0,1)^2\) and it converges to the original pair.  Choose bounded log-odds differences \(\delta_{a,x}^{(\varepsilon)}\in[-\log\Gamma_a,\log\Gamma_a]\) converging to each identified limiting difference; where a latent cell is null, choose any convergent value because that conditional margin carries vanishing mass.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) supplies the unique intercept which preserves exactly the observed risk \(r_{a,x}\).  The resulting conditional risks are in \((0,1)\) and their probability tables converge to the original nonnull margins.  Finally, every binary coupling of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) with given marginals is indexed by its \((1,1)\)-cell in the closed Fréchet interval; choosing an interior point of the corresponding perturbed interval and letting it converge to the original cell produces strictly positive conditional joint tables.  Use the same conditional coupling for both treatment values.  This preserves latent ignorability, while Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}observed\text{-}margin}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) preserve the observed law.  These positive tables belong to \(\mathcal M^\circ\) and converge to the given table.  Hence \(C\subseteq\mathcal M\), proving the asserted closed-table characterization without evaluating an odds ratio at a null cell.

Fix \(x\).  Under any \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^\circ\), Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}observed\text{-}margin}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}ignorability}\) give
\[
r_{a,x}
=\widetilde E\{Y(a)\mid A=a,X=x\}
=(1-w_{a,x})\mu_{a,0,x}+w_{a,x}\mu_{a,1,x}.
\]
Because \(p_x\in(0,1)\), Bayes' rule gives
\[
\pi_x=\widetilde P(U=1\mid X=x)
=p_xw_{1,x}+(1-p_x)w_{0,x}.
\]
After cancelling the positive observed treatment margins, the two treatment joint-cell inequalities are exactly the two inequalities defining \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) identifies \(\mu_{a,0,x}\) with \(\kappa(r_{a,x},w_{a,x},\theta_{a,x})\) and identifies \(\mu_{a,1,x}\) with its odds tilt.  Therefore
\[
\widetilde E\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}
=(1-\pi_x)\mu_{a,0,x}+\pi_x\mu_{a,1,x}
=q_{a,x}(w_{0,x},w_{1,x};\theta_{a,x}).
\]
The outcome inequalities imply \(\theta_{a,x}\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]\), and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) proves
\[
H_x^-(w_{0,x},w_{1,x})
\leq \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}
\leq H_x^+(w_{0,x},w_{1,x}).
\]
Minimizing and maximizing over the same posterior pair and then summing with the positive stratum masses gives the outer inclusion
\[
L\leq\tau(\widetilde P)\leq R.
\]

We next prove attainability rather than defining it.  Select in every stratum a pair \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\) and outcome odds \(\theta_{a,x}\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]\).  If these values are interior, set
\[
\widetilde P(A=1,U=1\mid X=x)=p_xw_{1,x},
\qquad
\widetilde P(A=0,U=1\mid X=x)=(1-p_x)w_{0,x},
\]
with the two \(U=0\) cells supplied by the fixed treatment margins.  These four numbers are positive and sum to one.  Use Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) to define \(\mu_{a,0,x},\mu_{a,1,x}\), and, conditional on \((X=x,U=u)\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently as Bernoulli variables with those two margins; use this same conditional law at both treatment values.  This last step gives \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid(X,U)\).  The mixture equations give the observed risks exactly, consistency gives the observed \(Y\), and the odds inequalities follow from the selected treatment pair and outcome odds.  Thus the constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal M^\circ\) and realizes the two displayed \(q\)-means simultaneously through one common \(U\).

The set \(D_{A,x}\) is connected.  On \((0,1)^2\), the coordinate transformation \((w_0,w_1)\mapsto(\operatorname{logit}w_0,\operatorname{logit}w_1)\) sends it to the convex strip
\[
\left|\operatorname{logit}w_1-operatorname{logit}w_0\right|
\leq\log\Gamma_A,
\]
and \(D_{A,x}\) is the closure of that strip's inverse image, with the constant-(U) corners added.  Consequently the product of \(D_{A,x}\) and the two outcome-odds intervals is connected.  The stratum contrast is continuous by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\), so its image is an interval.  Its endpoints are exactly \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\), because Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) first optimizes each outcome-odds interval and compactness then optimizes the common pair.  Independent selection across the finitely many strata makes the set of weighted sums the interval
\[
\left[\sum_x\lambda_x\ell_x,\sum_x\lambda_x\upsilon_x\right]=[L,R].
\]

If a selected pair lies on the boundary, Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}rr\text{-}bounded\text{-}union}\) supplies positive compatible laws converging to its probability table, and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) makes their contrasts converge to the selected value.  The limit belongs to \(\mathcal M\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\); hence both endpoints, and by connected interpolation every intermediate value, are attained over \(\mathcal M\).  Since \(\mathcal M^\circ\) is dense in \(\mathcal M\) by the same definition and \(\tau\) is linear and continuous on the finite simplex, its infimum and supremum over \(\mathcal M^\circ\) are \(L\) and \(R\), and the closure of its image is \([L,R]\).  Actual interior endpoint attainment occurs exactly when an attaining construction is strictly positive.  Finally, at a fixed interior tuple the preceding two applications of the law of total probability are precisely the Rosenbaum--Rubin fixed-parameter recalculation; no optimization or additional identifying equality is inserted into that fixed-tuple formula.

Fix a stratum and suppress \(x\).  All input numbers are rational, all budgets are finite, and \(p,r_0,r_1\in(0,1)\).  For each \(a\) and each legal endpoint \(\vartheta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}\), introduce a variable \(z_a\) and the polynomial
\[
F_a(w_a,z_a;\vartheta)
=(1-w_a)(\vartheta-1)z_a^2+\bigl[1+(w_a-r_a)(\vartheta-1)\bigr]z_a-r_a.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) proves that the additional inequalities
\[
0<z_a<1,
\qquad
1+(\vartheta-1)z_a>0
\]
select exactly one root of \(F_a=0\).  Therefore adjoining \(z_a\) is an exact semialgebraic graph construction, not a relaxation.  On that graph, \(m_{a,1}=\vartheta z_a/\{1+(\vartheta-1)z_a\}\) and every objective is rational with a denominator whose sign is known to be positive.

By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\), the signs of \(\pi-w_a\) choose the analytic endpoint formula for each \(q_a^-\) and \(q_a^+\).  The algorithm partitions \(D_A\) by the two affine sign polynomials \(\pi-w_a\), retains the equality faces as separate strata, and treats \(\Gamma_a=1\) by identifying the coincident endpoint branches.  Thus there are finitely many legal analytic branches.

For \(\Gamma_A>1\), the non-corner boundary of \(D_A\) consists of the two algebraic arcs
\[
w_1(1-w_0)=\Gamma_Aw_0(1-w_1),
\qquad
w_0(1-w_1)=\Gamma_Aw_1(1-w_0),
\]
together with their endpoints \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\).  The algorithm substitutes a rational parametrization of each arc, intersects it with every analytic sign stratum, and includes all resulting endpoints.  It also evaluates the two constant-\(U\) corners directly, where Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) gives \(q_a=r_a\).  When \(\Gamma_A=1\), subtraction of the two defining inequalities gives \(w_0=w_1\), so the algorithm instead optimizes on that diagonal.  These cases exhaust the topological boundary.

On the relative interior of every smooth branch, a local extremum either satisfies the two stationary equations or lies on a lower-dimensional branch face.  Implicit differentiation of \(F_a=0\) is legal because
\[
\frac{\partial F_a}{\partial z_a}
=\{1+(\vartheta-1)z_a\}
  \frac{d}{dz_a}\{(1-w_a)z_a+w_aT_\vartheta(z_a)\}>0,
\]
where positivity follows from the derivative calculation in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\).  Clearing the known positive denominators turns the stationary equations and the equations \(F_0=F_1=0\) into a finite polynomial system.  Saturation by the mixture denominators, arc denominators, Jacobian denominators, and branch-boundary polynomials removes precisely the components on which that clearing or that smooth-stratum derivation was illegal; those components have already been assigned to separate lower-dimensional strata.

For a zero-dimensional saturated system, successive resultants eliminate \(z_0,z_1\) and then one posterior coordinate.  Euclidean polynomial division terminates because degree strictly decreases.  The resulting univariate square-free factors have finitely many real roots.  Their signed-remainder sequences give exact rational isolating intervals: on an interval avoiding a remainder root, every sign is constant, and the difference in sign-variation counts at its endpoints equals the number of distinct roots; repeated bisection therefore isolates every root.  Back-substitution followed by rational interval Newton contraction certifies a unique solution box when the Jacobian is nonsingular.  Every box is then tested against the original, uncleared equations and inequalities, so a wrong quadratic branch or a zero-denominator artifact is rejected.

If a resultant vanishes identically, a Jacobian loses rank, roots collide, or the stationary ideal has positive dimension, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) does not use the generic resultant list.  It invokes sign-invariant cylindrical decomposition of the finite polynomial family consisting of the original constraints, all branch polynomials, and the objective comparison polynomials.  This procedure terminates by induction on the number of variables: in one variable the preceding signed-remainder isolation produces finitely many points and intervals; at each projection step only finitely many coefficients, discriminants, and pairwise resultants are added; over every cell of the lower-dimensional decomposition these projection polynomials have fixed signs, so finitely many isolated sections and sectors lift it to the next dimension.  On each lifted cell the original signs are invariant.  Hence root collisions and stationary continua are returned as exact algebraic cells rather than discarded.

Exhaustiveness now follows from compactness and finite stratification.  A minimum or maximum exists by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\).  Its point is either in a zero-dimensional face, in the relative interior of a one-dimensional face where the tangential derivative vanishes, or in a two-dimensional smooth stratum where both derivatives vanish; if the relevant derivatives fail to define an isolated point, the cylindrical-decomposition case contains the entire singular or stationary component.  Thus every optimizer occurs on the enumerated list or cell.  Exact comparison of algebraic objective values is obtained by refining disjoint rational isolating intervals, or, at equality, by reducing their defining polynomials on the common algebraic cell.  Applying this finite procedure to \(H^-\) and \(H^+\) returns exact representations and membership certificates for \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\).  The construction uses the input as coefficients throughout and therefore proves only the stated fixed-input certificate, not a symbolic parameter atlas.

For every stratum and every \(d=(w_0,w_1)\in D_{A,x}\),
\[
q^-_{1,x}(d)-q^+_{0,x}(d)
\geq \min_{e\in D_{A,x}}q^-_{1,x}(e)
      -\max_{f\in D_{A,x}}q^+_{0,x}(f).
\]
Taking the minimum over \(d\) proves the stratum lower inequality.  Similarly,
\[
q^+_{1,x}(d)-q^-_{0,x}(d)
\leq \max_{e\in D_{A,x}}q^+_{1,x}(e)
      -\min_{f\in D_{A,x}}q^-_{0,x}(f),
\]
and taking the maximum proves the upper inequality.  Multiplication by \(\lambda_x>0\), summation, and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}envelope}\) give
\[
L_{\mathrm{sep}}\leq L\leq R\leq R_{\mathrm{sep}},
\qquad
\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}.
\]

We verify the witness rather than treating its definition as proof.  Its marginal confounder prevalence and treatment odds ratio are
\[
\pi=\frac12\frac45+\frac12\frac15=\frac12,
\qquad
\operatorname{OR}\left(\frac45,\frac15\right)
=\frac{(4/5)(4/5)}{(1/5)(1/5)}=16.
\]
The observed risks, outcome odds ratios, causal contrast, and nominal contrast are
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_1&=\frac45\frac{13}{20}+\frac15\frac1{20}=\frac{53}{100},
&\theta_1&=\frac{(13/20)(19/20)}{(1/20)(7/20)}=\frac{247}{7}<36,\\
r_0&=\frac15\frac45+\frac45\frac1{10}=\frac6{25},
&\theta_0&=\frac{(4/5)(9/10)}{(1/10)(1/5)}=36,\\
\tau(P^\star)&=\frac12\left(\frac{13}{20}+\frac1{20}-\frac45-\frac1{10}\right)=-\frac1{10},
&r_1-r_0&=\frac{29}{100}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Bayes' rule gives treatment probabilities \(4/5\) and \(1/5\) in the two \(U\)-levels.  Together with the strictly interior Bernoulli risks and their independent conditional coupling, this proves that \(P^\star\) is a strictly positive member of the maintained class.

It remains to certify, rather than assume, the four numerical extrema.  On the reverse exposure arc, exact rearrangement of
\(w_0(1-w_1)=16w_1(1-w_0)\) gives
\[
w_1=t,
\qquad
w_0=W(t)=\frac{16t}{1+15t},
\qquad
16w_0(1-w_1)-w_1(1-w_0)=255w_1(1-w_0)>0.
\]
For the lower branch, \(\pi-w_1>0\) and \(\pi-w_0<0\), so Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) gives \(H^-=q_1(1/36)-q_0(1/36)\); for the upper branch it gives \(H^+=q_1(36)-q_0(36)\).  Substitution in the two mixture polynomials and the tangential derivative produces the two primitive square-free degree-sixteen factors recorded in \(\mathcal C^\star\).  The signed-remainder variation counts are respectively \(8-7=1\) and \(7-6=1\) on the displayed rational \(t\)-boxes.  Back-substitution in \(F_1=F_0=0\) contracts to the displayed \(z_1,z_0\)-boxes, all of which lie strictly inside \((0,1)\); the positive-denominator test and the original inactive inequality above validate both roots.  Rational interval evaluation then gives
\[
-\frac{107500302}{10^9}\leq L\leq-\frac{107500301}{10^9},
\qquad
\frac{539509967}{10^9}\leq R\leq\frac{539509968}{10^9}.
\]
The exhaustive branch, endpoint, corner, and stationary-cell comparison prescribed and proved correct in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}complete\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}certificate}\) has strictly inferior rational interval bounds for every other legal candidate, so these isolated roots are the global extrema.  Complementing \(U\) supplies the symmetric attaining pairs and changes \(\vartheta\) to \(1/\vartheta\), without changing the objective values.

For the armwise relaxation, direct substitution of the four rational posterior pairs from \(\mathcal C^\star\) into the active arc identity, the legal mixture equation, and the corresponding \(q\)-formula yields
\[
L_{\mathrm{sep}}=\frac{94711}{277400}-\frac{2553}{5650}
=-\frac{3461701}{31346200},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sep}}=\frac{212689}{302600}-\frac{1797}{12475}
=\frac{84380923}{150997400}.
\]
The same exhaustive exact comparison proves these are the separate arm extrema.  In particular,
\[
L-L_{\mathrm{sep}}
\in\left[\frac{2934168}{10^9},\frac{2934170}{10^9}\right],
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sep}}-R
\in\left[\frac{19313713}{10^9},\frac{19313715}{10^9}\right],
\]
so both gaps are strictly positive.

Finally, the square-free factors, one-root Sturm counts, interval-Newton boxes, positive denominators, inactive-constraint slack, and strict objective comparison gaps persist under sufficiently small perturbations of the interior observed summaries and of the finite budgets.  The implicit-function calculation is legal because the certified interval-Newton Jacobians exclude zero.  The two selected algebraic branches and all competing compact cells therefore vary continuously locally, and each positive rational gap remains positive after shrinking the neighborhood.  This proves strict tightening on a relatively open neighborhood, not merely at a single numerical input.

The proof of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}complete\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}certificate}\) gives a finite polynomial description of every legal posterior pair, mixture root, analytic outcome-sign branch, stationary condition, and objective comparison.  To describe the lower endpoint parametrically, adjoin variables for the legal roots and a value \(s_x\) in each stratum, assert that a feasible point has objective \(s_x\), and assert that no feasible point on any branch has a smaller objective.  The latter assertion is a first-order formula over the ordered coefficient field generated by the observed summaries and the budget parameters.  The finite projection-and-lifting construction in that proof eliminates the quantified variables and partitions any compact budget box into finitely many cells on which all projection-polynomial signs are fixed.  On each cell the legal optimizer strata, their ties, and the algebraic formula for \(\ell_x\) are fixed.  Summing \(L=\sum_x\lambda_x\ell_x\) and adjoining \(L=0\) therefore produces a finite semialgebraic stratification of \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Because the defining polynomial family includes discriminants, Jacobian minors, branch boundaries, and the constant-(U) faces, its lower-dimensional cells contain every optimizer tie, legal-root collision, constant-(U) contact, and positive-dimensional stationary continuum.

We next prove the monotonicity and continuity claims directly.  If \(\Gamma_A'\geq\Gamma_A\), each defining inequality for \(D_{A,x}(\Gamma_A)\) remains valid with \(\Gamma_A'\), so
\[
D_{A,x}(\Gamma_A)\subseteq D_{A,x}(\Gamma_A').
\]
If \(\Gamma_1'\geq\Gamma_1\), the interval over which the treated-arm minimum is taken expands, hence \(q_{1,x}^-\) cannot increase.  If \(\Gamma_0'\geq\Gamma_0\), the interval over which the control-arm maximum is taken expands, hence \(q_{0,x}^+\) cannot decrease.  Minimization over the enlarged exposure region then proves that \(L\) is coordinatewise nonincreasing in all three budgets.

For continuity in \(\Gamma_A\), put \(c=\log\Gamma_A\).  Away from the two constant corners, logit coordinates identify \(D_{A,x}\) with \(|t_1-t_0|\leq c\).  If \(c_n\to c>0\), any point can be approximated in the neighboring strip by keeping \((t_0+t_1)/2\) fixed and multiplying \(t_1-t_0\) by \(\min(1,c_n/c)\); the constant corners belong to every region.  If \(c=0\), use the common midpoint, which converges to the diagonal.  Conversely, every convergent sequence of feasible pairs has a feasible limit by the closed polynomial inequalities.  Hence these compact regions converge in Hausdorff distance.  The mixture and endpoint objectives are jointly continuous in posterior pairs and finite budgets by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\), including at \(\Gamma_a=1\).  Uniform continuity on a common compact neighborhood and the elementary inequalities obtained by evaluating each minimum at a nearby feasible point show that every \(\ell_x\), and hence \(L\), is continuous.

For rational or real-algebraic summaries and box endpoints, all projection coefficients are effective elements of \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\).  Euclidean remainder sequences, algebraic-number sign tests, and the finite projection-and-lifting recursion therefore terminate and return exact quantifier-free sign cells.  A zero-dimensional specialization admits rational root isolation by the signed-remainder argument; a positive-dimensional cell is instead returned by its exact algebraic sign description, so no nonexistent rational interval is promised.  This is exactly the output contract of \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\), distinct from the fixed-input output of \(\mathsf{CERT}\).

If \(\Gamma_A=1\), the two inequalities defining \(D_{A,x}\) are opposite weak inequalities and hence give equality:
\[
w_1(1-w_0)=w_0(1-w_1).
\]
After cancellation this is \(w_1=w_0\), including the boundary values.  Consequently \(\pi_x=p_xw_1+(1-p_x)w_0=w_{a,x}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\), or directly Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}adjusted\text{-}arm\text{-}mean}\), gives
\[
q_{a,x}=r_{a,x}+(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(m_1-m_0)=r_{a,x}.
\]
Thus \(H_x^-=H_x^+=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}\), and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}envelope}\) yields
\[
L=R=\sum_x\lambda_x(r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}).
\]

If \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\), the two outcome inequalities are equalities.  On the positive chart their ratio calculation in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) gives \(\theta_{a,x}=1\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) then gives
\[
\mu_{a,0,x}=\kappa(r_{a,x},w_{a,x},1)=r_{a,x},
\qquad
\mu_{a,1,x}=r_{a,x}.
\]
Hence again \(q_{a,x}=r_{a,x}\) for every feasible posterior pair.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) carries this equality to all boundary pairs in the closed class, and the same sharp-envelope calculation gives the asserted point-identification formula.

First derive a budget-free outer bound from consistency alone.  In stratum \(x\), for some \(s_{1,x},s_{0,x}\in[0,1]\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde E\{Y(1)\mid X=x\}
&=p_xr_{1,x}+(1-p_x)s_{1,x},\\
\widetilde E\{Y(0)\mid X=x\}
&=(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+p_xs_{0,x}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore every compatible law, and in particular every law in every finite-budget common-(U) class, obeys
\[
p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}-p_x
\leq \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}
\leq p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+1-p_x.
\]
After weighting and summing, this gives a lower bound on \(L\) and an upper bound on \(R\) equal to the two claimed Manski endpoints.

It remains to show that both inequalities become attainable in the all-budget limit through the same binary confounder.  Along any sequence with \(\Gamma_{A,n},\Gamma_{0,n},\Gamma_{1,n}\to\infty\), choose in each stratum
\[
\varepsilon_n=\frac{1}{1+\sqrt{\Gamma_{A,n}}},
\qquad
w_{1,x}^{(n)}=1-\varepsilon_n,
\qquad
w_{0,x}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_n.
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{OR}(w_{1,x}^{(n)},w_{0,x}^{(n)})
=\frac{(1-\varepsilon_n)^2}{\varepsilon_n^2}=\Gamma_{A,n},
\qquad
\pi_x^{(n)}\longrightarrow p_x.
\]
Bayes' rule consequently gives \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=1,X=x)\to1\) and \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=0,X=x)\to0\), so latent positivity vanishes along this sequence.

For the lower endpoint select \(\theta_{1,x}^{(n)}=\Gamma_{1,n}\) and \(\theta_{0,x}^{(n)}=\Gamma_{0,n}\).  In the treated mixture, \(w_{1,x}^{(n)}\to1\), so
\[
|\mu_{1,1,x}^{(n)}-r_{1,x}|
\leq1-w_{1,x}^{(n)}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Since \(\operatorname{odds}(\mu_{1,0,x}^{(n)})=operatorname{odds}(\mu_{1,1,x}^{(n)})/\Gamma_{1,n}\), interiority of \(r_{1,x}\) implies \(\mu_{1,0,x}^{(n)}\to0\).  In the control mixture, \(w_{0,x}^{(n)}\to0\), so \(\mu_{0,0,x}^{(n)}\to r_{0,x}\), while
\(\operatorname{odds}(\mu_{0,1,x}^{(n)})=Gamma_{0,n}\operatorname{odds}(\mu_{0,0,x}^{(n)})\) implies \(\mu_{0,1,x}^{(n)}\to1\).  Hence the common-pair lower contrast converges to
\[
p_xr_{1,x}-\{(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+p_x\}.
\]

For the upper endpoint select \(\theta_{1,x}^{(n)}=\Gamma_{1,n}^{-1}\) and \(\theta_{0,x}^{(n)}=\Gamma_{0,n}^{-1}\).  The same mixture argument gives
\[
\mu_{1,1,x}^{(n)}\to r_{1,x},\quad
\mu_{1,0,x}^{(n)}\to1,quad
\mu_{0,0,x}^{(n)}\to r_{0,x},\quad
\mu_{0,1,x}^{(n)}\to0,
\]
and therefore the common-pair upper contrast converges to
\[
p_xr_{1,x}+1-p_x-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}.
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}envelope}\) places \(L_n\) below the first feasible contrasts and \(R_n\) above the second, while the consistency bound places them on the opposite sides.  The squeeze theorem and the finite weighted sum over \(x\) prove convergence to the displayed interval.  The construction explicitly uses diverging budgets and propensities conditional on \(U\) tending to zero or one, so it yields no finite-budget or uniform-latent-positivity recovery claim.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniform confidence regions across legal-root collisions and positive-dimensional stationary continua, together with the exact stochastic directional law on each such singular stratum, remain open.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core specifies no sampling regularity, influence functions, nuisance-rate conditions, covariance nondegeneracy, or bootstrap coupling.  More importantly, at a root collision the active algebraic set itself changes with the observed-law direction, while at a stationary continuum its support functional can have a non-finite active index set.  The regular finite-branch delta calculation therefore does not imply uniform coverage over those strata.
open_obligations.attempted: Implicit differentiation closes unique nonsingular branches, and finite minima or maxima close finite regular ties.  Extending the same route to a colliding or positive-dimensional stationary set fails because neither a uniform metric expansion of the moving feasible correspondence nor an anti-concentration bound for the resulting Gaussian support functional is available from the stated primitives.
open_obligations.partial_result: On a regular branch with a unique optimizer and nonsingular stationary Jacobian, the implicit-function calculation used by \(\mathsf{CERT}\) makes \(L\) and \(R\) differentiable functions of the finite vector \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})_{x\in\mathcal X}\).  At a finite tie of regular branches, the directional derivative of a minimum is the minimum of the tied branch derivatives, and the derivative of a maximum is their maximum.  These deterministic facts identify the candidate pointwise Gaussian directional limits once an asymptotically linear law for the observed-summary estimator is supplied.  They do not establish uniform validity near colliding roots or stationary continua.
